parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence is recorded, and sexuality conduct was decriminalised in 2021 with an orientation anti-discrimination statute, though gender identity is not clearly covered. No border, facility or visitor-specific rule is documented; border treatment is an open question, weighted lightly. The main known exposure is a June 2024 case of police attacking, detaining and degrading a trans woman because of her identity, state-implicated but a single incident under investigation. A 2024 shadow report documents discrimination in health, education and employment, but without itemised incidents, so its weight is limited. Custody placement is undocumented, and no violence counts or baseline are given. Survey support (49%) and the 2012 visible-star case are modest acceptance signals. Gender-marker absence is resident-facing and not scored. Net: thin, mixed evidence with a documented state-police exposure, placing it at the Elevated/Reduced boundary.
